correctness.rationale: A trial point \(\alpha=(3\delta)^{-1}\) gives an \(O(\sqrt\delta)\) excess above one half. Any minimizer must have \(\alpha\to\infty\); the uniform first-order Gamma transition approximation then forces \(z=\delta\sqrt\alpha\to0\). The bound \(h_\kappa(\alpha)-1/2\ge c z-C/\sqrt\alpha\), compared with the trial value, gives an upper bound on \(r=\delta\alpha\); the same expansion rules out \(r\to0\), so minimizers localize in a compact subset of \((0,\infty)\). There the supplied differentiable transition expansion is uniform. Writing \(\varepsilon=\sqrt\delta\) gives \(1/2+\phi(0)\varepsilon A(r)+\phi(0)\varepsilon^3B(r)+O(\varepsilon^4)\), with \(A(r)=\sqrt r+1/(3\sqrt r)\) uniquely minimized at \(r=1/3\). Independent symbolic differentiation reproduced \(A(1/3)=2\sqrt3/3\), \(A''(1/3)=3\sqrt3/2\), \(B(1/3)=-71\sqrt3/270\), and \(B'(1/3)=-7\sqrt3/30\), hence the shift \(-B'/A''=7/45\) and the stated minimum expansion. The package's \(\kappa=1.01\) numerical check agrees but is only supporting evidence.
